segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Okay, I think we're all here. Thanks for jumping on. The goal today is simple: lock the plan for the beta launch of the Panfold app, and leave with names next to every open item.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Sounds good. Before we start, I should say up front that the sync bug isn't fixed yet. Recipes saved offline still sometimes show up twice when the phone reconnects.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: How bad is it?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: About one in twenty test devices. It's annoying, not dangerous. Nobody loses a recipe, they just see a duplicate. But I wouldn't want two hundred strangers seeing it on day one.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Can we launch with it and fix it in the first update?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: We could, but the fix is small. I think it's two days of work. I'd rather ship without it.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Then that's the first commitment. Daniel, you'll have the duplicate-recipe fix in by Friday?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Yes, Friday. If it slips, I'll tell you Wednesday, not Friday night.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Perfect. Which brings us to the date. We said May sixth. With the fix landing Friday and a few days of testing after, the sixth feels tight.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: It does. And honestly, the sixth is a Wednesday right after a holiday weekend for some of our testers. The thirteenth would be better for me anyway. It gives me a full week for the invite email.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: The thirteenth works for engineering.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Okay, decision: the beta moves from May sixth to May thirteenth. I'll update the plan doc after this call.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Next is the size of the beta. We talked about five hundred people. I'd still like five hundred.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I'd push back on that. Support is basically me and Maya answering emails. Five hundred people in the first week is a lot of email.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: What would you be comfortable with?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Two hundred. Then open it up in waves.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: My worry is that two hundred isn't enough to learn anything about which recipes people actually cook. The whole point of the beta is the weekly plan feature, and we need people using it for a few weeks.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: That's fair. What if we start at two hundred, and if support is quiet after two weeks, we add another three hundred?

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I can live with that, as long as the second wave actually happens and doesn't quietly disappear.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: It won't. Decision: the beta starts with two hundred people, with a second wave of three hundred after two weeks if support volume is manageable. Rosa, can you own the waitlist and decide who goes in which wave?

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Yes, I'll own the waitlist.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Great. Daniel, platforms. Are we doing Android in the beta?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I'd say no. The Android build works, but the share sheet is broken and the notifications are unreliable. iPhone only for the beta, Android in the summer.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: About forty percent of the waitlist is on Android, though.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I know. But a bad first impression on Android is worse than a short wait.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: I agree with Daniel here. Decision: the beta is iPhone only. Rosa, we'll need a line in the invite email for the Android people so they don't feel forgotten.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I'll write that. Something like: "Android is coming this summer, and you'll be first in line."

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Good. That leads to the invite email itself. When can we see a draft?

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I'll have a draft to you by Wednesday. It'll include the Android line and the date change.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: By Wednesday, to me. Got it. And I'll review it the same day.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: One thing on the email: please don't promise the meal-plan export. It's not going to be in the beta.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Noted. No export in the email.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Let's talk about learning from the beta. I want real conversations, not just a survey. I'll book five user interviews for the second week of the beta, thirty minutes each.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Can I sit in on a couple?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Of course. I'll send you the times when they're booked.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: And I'd like the crash reports going to the shared channel, not just my inbox. I'll set that up before launch.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Thank you. So the open question I don't want to lose is pricing after the beta. Do we charge from day one when the beta ends, or give beta users a free period?

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I'd give them three free months. They're doing us a favor.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I don't have a strong view, but I'd want to know the cost first.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: I don't think we can decide this today without numbers. Let's leave pricing open and come back to it next week, when I've got the cost estimate.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Fine by me.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Okay, let me read back what we've got. Decisions: the beta moves to May thirteenth; it starts with two hundred people, with a second wave of three hundred after two weeks if support is manageable; and it's iPhone only, with Android in the summer. Commitments: Daniel fixes the duplicate-recipe bug by Friday and warns us by Wednesday if it slips. Daniel also sends crash reports to the shared channel before launch. Rosa owns the waitlist, and sends me the invite email draft by Wednesday, with the Android line, the new date, and no mention of export. I update the plan doc today, review Rosa's draft the same day it arrives, and book five user interviews for the second week. Open: pricing after the beta, next week.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: That's everything from my side.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Same here.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Great. Thanks, both. Talk Friday.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Thanks, both. One week from the planning call, and the beta opens in six days. Let's go through where we are.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Good news first. The duplicate-recipe fix went in on Thursday, a day early. We ran it on all twenty test devices over the weekend, no duplicates.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: That's great. And the crash reports to the shared channel?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: That one slipped. I started it, but the setup needs an admin login I don't have yet. I'll have it done by Monday.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Monday is two days before launch. Is that safe?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: It's safe. If it isn't working by Monday afternoon, I'll forward the reports by hand during the first week.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Okay. Rosa, the invite email?

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Sent you the draft on Wednesday, like I said. It has the new date, the Android line, and nothing about export.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: I read it the same day. It's good. I made two small edits and sent it back, so it's ready to schedule.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: Great. I'll schedule it for Monday morning. But I want to raise Android again. Since the email went to a few early testers, three people have replied asking why they can't join on their phones. All three are on Android.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I hear that, but nothing has changed on our side. The share sheet is still broken.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I'm not asking to change the decision. I'm asking for a date. "This summer" is vague, and these are exactly the people who'll tell their friends.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: That's fair. Daniel, can you give us a month by next week's call?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I can give you a month by next week, yes.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Good. Then pricing. I said I'd come back with the cost estimate, and I have it. Running the app for two hundred people costs us very little; it's the meal-plan servers, and they're cheap at this size.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: So three free months is fine?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Three free months is fine. Decision: beta users get three months free after the beta ends, then the normal price. I'll write that into the plan doc today.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Works for me.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: I'll add a line about it to the welcome email, not the invite.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Good. Last thing, the second wave. If support is quiet after two weeks we add three hundred. Who decides whether it's quiet?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I'd say: fewer than ten support emails a day in the second week.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: That's a clear line. Agreed.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Decision: the second wave goes ahead if the second week averages fewer than ten support emails a day. Okay, read-back. Done since last week: the duplicate fix, the invite draft and my review. Slipped: crash reports, now Monday. New decisions: three free months after the beta, and the ten-email rule for the second wave. Commitments: Daniel gives us an Android month by next week; Rosa schedules the invite for Monday and adds the pricing line to the welcome email; I update the plan doc today.

segments.speaker: rosa
segments.text: That's it from me.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Same.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Thanks, both.
